question: does one linear mission-time curve F(t) reproduce the gen1 per-swath constants, and does it make the two Elba tiles agree about the same flight lines?

inputs.role: per-swath gps_time window, midpoint and return count, from the gen1 LAZ files
elba: saved per-swath (dx,dy,dz), along-track drift curves, stable 1-sigma
elbaext: saved per-swath (dx,dy,dz), along-track drift curves, stable 1-sigma
whitewater: saved per-swath (dx,dy,dz), along-track drift curves, stable 1-sigma
mnrv: saved per-swath (dx,dy,dz), along-track drift curves, stable 1-sigma
cook: saved per-swath (dx,dy,dz), along-track drift curves, stable 1-sigma
carlton: saved per-swath (dx,dy,dz), along-track drift curves, stable 1-sigma
battlecreek: saved per-swath (dx,dy,dz), along-track drift curves, stable 1-sigma

params.name: swath_reference
params.why: align_swaths gauge in pipeline.difference_dem; that swath is pinned to zero and is excluded from every fit below

columns.axis: dz (mm), dx (m) or dy (m) -- the alignment component being modelled
columns.nsw: swaths in the fit (the forced-zero reference swath excluded)
columns.rate: fitted F rate: mm/hour for dz, m/hour for dx and dy
columns.rms_time: RMS residual of F linear in gps_time to the saved constants (mm or m)
columns.rms_ord: RMS residual of F linear in flight-line ordinal, same units
columns.max_time: largest absolute residual of the gps_time model (mm or m)
columns.p_now: free parameters of the current model on this axis: n swaths minus the gauge
columns.p_Ft: free parameters of linear F on this axis after the gauge: 1 (the rate)
columns.stable_sigma_mm: stable_1sigma_m from the site's corrections.json, mm
columns.swath: point_source_id shared by the two Elba tiles
columns.obs_mm: observed elbaext-minus-elba dz for that swath, both re-referenced to 135, mm
columns.Ft_mm: the same difference predicted by each tile's own fitted F(t), mm
columns.Fk_mm: the same difference predicted by each tile's own fit linear in swath id, mm
columns.rms_mm: RMS over the shared swaths, mm
columns.pair: consecutive pair of swaths in time order
columns.gap_h: elapsed time between consecutive swath midpoints, hours
columns.obs_h: hours of the gap in which returns actually exist (the two 45-60 s windows)
columns.frac_obs: obs_h / gap_h -- the fraction of the interval F(t) is constrained on
columns.drift_pp_mm: peak-to-peak of the saved WITHIN-swath along-track drift curve, mm
columns.drift_rate_mm_h: drift_pp_mm divided by the swath's own duration, mm/hour
columns.between_rate_mm_h: the site's fitted BETWEEN-swath rate, mm/hour, for comparison

headline: single-curve mission-time model fitted and compared with the per-swath constants
